description.narrative: Insatsen utgör ett stöd till fem OECD-DAC nätverk, vars respektive inriktning går hand i hand med de fem perspektiv som ska genomsyra Sidas arbete enligt myndighetens instruktion. Nätverkens aktiviteter ska bidra till DAC:s övergripande mål som under 2018-2022 är att främja utvecklingssamarbete och andra relevanta policyer så att dessa bidrar till genomförandet av Agenda 2030 för hållbar utveckling, inklusive hållbar och inkluderande ekonomisk tillväxt, fattigdomsbekämpning, förbättring av levnadsstandarden i utvecklingsländer och en framtid där inget land är beroende av bistånd. Nätverken bedöms vara viktiga plattformar för lärande, innovation och nytt tänkande inom det internationella utvecklingssamarbetet. Genom att stödja genomförandet av nätverkens aktiviteter bidrar Sida till DAC:s övergripande mål samt de fem policyutmaningar som listas i DAC:s arbetsprogram och budget för 2023-2025.

Support to five OECD-DAC networks with thematic focus areas that overlap with the five perspectives must permeate Sida’s operations according to instructions from the Swedish government. The activities of the networks will contribute to the fulfillment of DAC’s overall goals for 2018-2022 to promote development cooperation and other relevant policies so that these contribute to the implementation of Agenda 2030 for sustainable development, including sustainable and inclusive economic growth, poverty reduction, improvement of living standards in developing countries, and a future in which no country is dependent on aid. The networks are considered to be important platforms for learning, innovation and creative thinking in international development cooperation. By supporting the implementation of network activities, Sida contributes to the fulfillment of DAC’s overall goals as well as the five policy challenges listed in DAC's work program and budget for 2023-2025.

Övergripande mål och förväntade resultat för DAC:s arbetsprogram och budget för 2023-2024 är indelade i tre övergripande områden: 1) Medvetenhet/förståelse - inklusive ökad förståelse för bland annat globala utvecklingstrender, multidimensionell fattigdom och utvecklingspolicy; 2) Tillämpning/användning - inklusive ökat användande av evidens och statistik inklusive användande av TotalTOSSD (Official Support for Sustainable Development) standard och rapporteringsramverk; 3) Effekter - bland annat i form av bibehållen integritet för att hålla medlemmar ansvariga, att medlemmar anpassar sina policyer och system till rådande verkligheter och utmaningar och är bättre rustade för att uppnå och följa upp resultat.
De fem tematiska nätverk bidrar till de övergripande målen med följande förväntade resultat:
3.1. INCAF
DAC-medlemmar får bättre kunskap och förståelse för multidimensionell fattigdom och skörhet (fragility) genom förbättrad tillgång till data och analys av sköra kontexter, inklusive bättre omfattning, storlek och timing för insatser med fokus på kris/konfliktförebyggande, fred och motståndskraft. (Effekter)
DAC-medlemmar förbättrar sin effektivitet och resultat i instabila och krissituationer genom mer evidensbaserade insatser, bland annat genom genomförandet av DAC Rekommendation om kopplingen mellan humanitärt bistånd, utveckling och fred. (Effekter)
4.1 GENDERNET
DAC-medlemmar är rustade för att leverera resultat av jämställdhetsåtaganden och kvinnors och flickors rättigheter med en förbättrad evidensbas för att genomföra mer systematiska, påskyndade åtgärder. Effektiviteten ökar genom att jämställdhetsfrågor integreras i alla sektorer och genom att man stöder särskilda statliga prioriteringar för jämställdhet samt att man tar itu med den alltmer akuta oron över ökande fattigdom och ojämlikhet. (Tillämpning/användning)
Effektivt stöd för implementeringen av DAC-rekommendationen om att stoppa sexuellt utnyttjande, övergrepp och trakasserier samt ökad efterlevnad från internationella organisationer, utvecklingsbanker och icke-medlemmar. (Tillämpning/användning)
4.2 Governance (GOVNET)
DAC-medlemmar är bättre informerade och rustade för att stödja partnerländerna i arbetet med öppna och inkluderande samhällen, säkerställa integritet och ansvarsskyldighet vid mobilisering och användning av finansiella resurser för hållbar utveckling (inbegripet ODA och mobilisering av inhemska resurser) och fullgöra sina globala klimatförändringsåtaganden. (Medvetenhet/förståelse).
4.3 Community of Practice Poverty and Inequalities (CoP-PI)
Förbättrad kvalitet, effektivitet och effekter av politik, praxis och finansiering för utvecklingssamarbete när det gäller att minska fattigdomen och ojämlikhet för att göra konkreta framsteg med löftet att inte lämna någon utanför, vilket blivit allt viktigare sedan pandemin och krigeti Ukraina. (Effekter)
5.1 Climate, Environment, Biodiversity and Sustainable Oceans (ENVIRONET)
Medlemmarna ges stöd i genomförandet av OECD/DAC-deklarationen om en ny strategi för att anpassa utvecklingssamarbetet med målen i Parisavtalet om klimatförändringar. (Tillämpning/användning).

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution
Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
Utvalda resultat från de respektive nätverken taget från OECD-DACs slutrapportering:
INCAF
Development and peace peace and ODA published. A workshop on Development-Peace coordination, conflict prevention in Coastal West Africa with UNOCHA), (7 Nov 2023) and at DCAF International partner forum (6 Dec 2023). In 2024, this workstream gained strength, Workshop in Washington on WB fragility Forum -" finding peace in the Nexus" (Feb) at the SIPRI Forum (May), ISSAT (June) , ODI (October) - All events led to Agreement to start in 2025 the review of the 2008 OECD handbook on Security Sector Reform/Governance, and to organise an OECD Forum on Development and peace early 2025.
Economies in conflict Partnership and engagement started to support a HDP Nexus approach to Staying engaged on critical economic issues and basic services in fragile and conflictaffected countries and on Private sector development and partnerships in fragile and conflictaffected contexts. Event at the Africa Resilience Forum with the African Development Bank (3 Oct 2023).
Humanitarian Development Peace Nexus Coordination across the Nexus published in December 2023.and The humanitarian-development-peace nexus and forced displacement in November 2024. The Nexus helpdesk function of the INCAF Secretariat allowed to support DAC members on Nexus related issues (workshops across government, review of draft strategies). A financing strategy methodology was elaborated in 2023 to support the financing workstream of the DAC-UN dialogue on the HDP Nexus. During the reporting period, the coordination across the HDP Nexus monitoring of the implementation of the DAC Recommendation on the HP Nexus was also drafted, being released in Q1 2024.
Forced displacement: Publication of two policy documents to explore the potential and challenges of the social and economic inclusion of forcibly displaced. Refugees and internally displaced persons in development planning; and The role of political will in enabling long-term development approaches to forced displacement in March 2024, in order to bring attention to the political dimension of integration of forcibly displaced persons. Page 3 of 3 A Common position Addressing Forced Displacement with a Comprehensive HumanitarianDevelopment-Peace Nexus Approach was adopted in Nov 2023 in order to steer a HDP nexus to forced displacement. The Common position was also endorsed by non DAC members and international organisations as a contribution to the Global refugee Forum in December 2023.
Climate change and fragility: Leading up to the COP28, a series of research and policy paper were elaborated, in particular on climate financing to fragile contexts Cooling the hotspot as well as Where ODA meets peace, climate and environmental goals (unpublished) and Biodiversity and fragility. Alongside the INCAF Common Position on climate change, biodiversity and environmental fragility , this research fed into the preparation of the DAC HighLevel Roundtable at COP28 on Climate Action and Finance in Fragile and Conflict-affected Contexts.
CoP-PI
- Stronger connections between P&I experts across DAC members. - Enhanced dialogue and learning on key challenges and solutions in reducing P&I through development co-operation among DAC members and a broader community, including experts from other providers, partner countries, academia and civil society. - Increased knowledge on DAC members approaches to addressing P&I and on development co-operations role in tackling these issues. This will serve as foundation for the up-coming OECD Guidance to Reduce P&I through Development Co-operation. - Heightened attention to P&I reduction issues at the DAC and in other international spaces (including at UNGA 2023 and through OECD inputs to the G20 process). This will be further secured going forward through continued CoP-PI events, and the production of the Guidance.
Environet
- The OECD has consolidated its role as the main provider of data and analysis on development finance on biodiversity, including the statistical reports and dialogue through the DAC Friends of Biodiversity Group . Secretariat work feature in the media, e.g. Bloomberg, Les Échos, Carbon Pulse, Reuters, The Guardian, etc. Finally, the work is also mentioned in other influential reports used for CBD negotiations and/or to disseminate the work with the media, namely: the dashboard of the 10 Point Plan on Financing Biodiversity, the CBD Secretariat to Campaign for Nature. - The ENVIRONET Secretariat worked with members and external stakeholders to develop a DAC approach to supporting net-zero energy transition, a key request from the DAC Declaration [DAC/CHAIR(2021)1/FINAL], The document was developed and approved by ENVIRONET in 2023-24, and approved by the DAC in February 2025 DCD/DAC(2025)8/FINAL. - The collaboration with the COP28 Presidency has provided a basis and reference for collaboration with future COP presidencies. DCD is in consultation with the Azeri COP29 presidencies regarding specific contributions and collaboration to support ambitious outcome. - Work on effective delivery of climate action has started to address the knowledge gap around the challenges and approaches for more effective delivery of climate action from the perspective of development partners practices, systems and approaches. It has informed the scope of the peer learning process for the work on Paris alignment and effectiveness and its related workshops, and is gathering momentum for a key DAC contribution on effective delivery of climate action. - The report on SIDS capacity to access finance continues provided key evidence and analysis in relation to SIDS priorities, including for the SIDS4 conference in Antigua and Barbuda in the week of 27 May 2024. o The capacity development in SIDS work has fed into the UKs House of Commons report that will advise the UK FCDO development co-operation policy on SIDS; and has also resulted in a request for contribution to the 2025 Global Center for Adaptation flagship report, to be launched at the SIDS Summit in May 2025. - The report Delivering on Climate Commitments: How DAC Members Are Aligning with the Goals of the Paris Agreement was approved by the DAC by the written procedure. The report responds to the commitments made in the DAC Declaration on a New Approach to Align Development Co-operation with the Goal of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and the specific mandate from the DAC High-Level Meeting in November 2023 for the preparation of a report. Key policy messages and findings from the report were presented back -to-back with the 2025 DAC High-Level Meeting in Paris and have informed the second peer learning workshop on Effective Delivery of Climate Action in May 2025. - The process of developing the Guidance for Development Co-operation in support of Sustainable Ocean Economies, generated a policy community on the Sustainable Ocean Economy across development co-operation providers, creating for the first time a common basis for a shared understanding on good practice. The process facilitated peer learning among the international ocean community and resulted in the first guidance on development co -operation for a sustainable ocean economy. The guidance was presented to, and subsequently approved by, the DAC in April 2025. It will be launched at the Third UN Ocean Conference in June 2025. - The Secretariats evidence base and data on the sustainable ocean economy have fed into and supported crucial ongoing international processes, such as the Finance in Common Summit, the upcoming Third UN Ocean Conference, and the ongoing the global plastics treaty negotiations. o Tracking of development assistance for the ocean economy and for curbing plastic pollution increased transparency of ocean-related development finance flows, including private finance mobilised for the ocean economy, highlighting areas of opportunity to scale up efforts or improve targeting. o Through the Blue Recovery Hubs, DCD provided policy support to small island developing states to build resilience through the ocean economy, including by identifying ocean-based industries that can act as engines of diversification and policy and financing solutions for integrated management of ocean resources. The Blue Recovery Hubs initiative was presented at the Our Ocean Conference 2024 in Greece.
Govnet
- The objective of the Networks work on ODA to different regime contexts is two-fold, to: increase members understanding, and awareness of the range of existing governance tools and approaches adopted to operate effectively in different regime contexts; and enhance multidisciplinary engagement on issues of ODA and autocratisation, making links to policy discussions on conflict and fragility, gender equality, development effectiveness and locally led development. Following the publication of the quantitative study on ODA to different regime contexts, in 2024 GovNet concluded a qualitative analysis of ten country cases, as reflected in a synthesis of country cases to better understand (a) if, and how, the composition of ODA flows to countries differs according to regime contexts; (b) how donors respond to changes in regime types, critical junctures and processes of democratisation and autocratisation; and (c) what factors shape these decisions, with reference to variables related to the country context and the policy and programmatic priorities of the donor. The results of those country case analyses are captured in a draft synthesis report titled ODA Flows to Different Regime Contexts. GovNet Secretariat has produced a draft policy synopsis titled Key Considerations When Delivering Aid to Different Regime Types detailing the policy dilemmas and potential policy and programmatic responses that could be adopted by ODA. Both documents were shared and discussed at the GovNet Plenary Meeting in November 2024.
- On media and the information environment, on 22 March 2024, the DAC approved the Development Co-operation Principles for Relevant and Effective Support to Media and the Information Environment. These Principles respond to the need to renew and update the 2014 OECD Principles on media assistance which no longer responded to the unprecedented challenges faced by free and independent media today, including increasing disinformation, polarisation and autocratisation, the rise of non - traditional media sources and growing threats to viability of med a business models. The Principles also seek to reinvigorate international support for PIM and inspire development co-operation providers to increase levels of financial and other forms of assistance in these areas. Alongside publication of the Principles, in June 2024, GovNet also published a Mapping of ODA to media and information environment integrity [DCD/DAC/GOVNET(2023)13]. This mapping analyses current trends, policies and practices in ODA to media and the information environment and incorporates the insights derived from a set of country case studies including Ukraine, Myanmar, Tanzania, the Western Balkans and global programmes.
- Under its workstream on Climate Change Adaptation Governance, a draft Synthesis Report on Climate Change Adaptation Governance[DCD/DAC/GOVNET(2024)22] was discussed at GovNets Plenary Meeting in November 2024. This Synthesis is accompanied by four background papers and includes a series of provisional policy recommendations on strategies to improve ODA to governance support in this area. Among the headline findings resulting from this work are that: i) the predominant focus of externally supported adaptation on national and regional biophysical climate risks is compromising effective responses to local socio-ecological realities and vulnerabilities; and 2) that high levels of fragmentation of adaptation governance across different scales of decision-making global, regional, national, domestic and local together with the politicisation of adaptation knowledge and resources are hampering the ability of climate exposed communities to derive the support they need.
Anti-Corruption Task Team - In terms of the monitoring of the 2016 Recommendation through DAC and WGB mechanisms, in Q3 and 4 2023 and in 2024, the Secretariat contributed to the DAC peer reviews of the Netherlands, Czechia, Poland, France, Slovenia, Finland and Luxembourg, to the UK mid-term review as well as to the WGB evaluation of Luxembourg, Türkiye, Sweden, South Africa, New Zealand, Croatia and Belgium.
- In line with members agreed roadmap to further support implementation of the Recommendation, the Secretariat moved forward with the policy brief series on Corruption Risk Management (CRM). Following the release of a first brief on under-reporting of suspected incidents of corruption in early 2023, the Secretariat finalised two policy briefs on corruption risk management (CRM): one on corruption as a development obstacle, and another on unpacking zero tolerance to corruption in 2024. A third draft policy brief on safeguarding the integrity of ODA was also prepared end of 2024.
- Following a request by members in the June 2024 plenary, the Secretariat conducted analysis on how to improving the tracking of ODA related to anti-corruption. It delivered an explainer note on options to track ODA related to anti-corruption in November 2024, and a follow-up note on the opportunities and constraints of an anti-corruption policy marker in December 2024.
- On Illicit Financial Flows (IFFs) and development,, the DAC published the first OECD/DAC Policy Guidance on Mitigating the Risks of Illicit Financial Flows in Oil Commodity Trading: Enabling integrity in the energy transition in August 2023. This guidance assists members to better use and deploy ODA resources to counter IFF risks in oil commodity trading, thus enabling more effective domestic resource mobilisation, reducing the risks of debt distress and enabling integrity in the energy transition, particularly carbon trading. The Policy Guidance was accompanied by three new papers: investigative journalism, oil commodity trading and addressing the risk of IFFs and governing through transparency.
Gendernet
- DAC Members, as shareholders in the multilateral system and catalysts for multi-stakeholder action, are equipped to deliver results on commitments to gender equality and womens empowerment and rights with an improved evidence base to implement more systematic, accelerated action, and; effectiveness of policies, programmes and investments is increased through the integration of gender issues across sectors, and work to support dedicated government priorities on gender equality; and increasingly acute concerns around rising poverty and inequalities are addressed. Notably, the Secretariat built the evidence base and support the adoption of a new DAC standard, the DAC Recommendation on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of All Women and Girls in 2024, and since the Secretariat continues to support the launch and implementation efforts of many members, providing support for events, training, communications, and featuring it in other venues, with multilateral organisa tions and development banks.
- Agenda-setting on gender equality issues advancing at all levels through the membership of the DAC Network on Gender Equality (GENDERNET), and with leaders and experts in partner countries, civil society, academia, the private sector, etc. One example involved background work and briefings to support political efforts, such as the inclusion of references in the UN Commission on the Status of Women 68 focused on financing for gender equality which pointed to the need for increased financing for gender equality in development assistance. The most inclusive session of the in-person meeting of the DAC Network on Gender Equality in 2024 led to increased engagement around all work areas and ideas for the effective implementation of the work program, it included representatives in leadership roles on gender equality from the multilateral organisations and development banks, foundations, the private sector, civil society/women -led organisations, and academia.
- Effective support for members efforts to work on better tracking financing for gender equality through analysis and use of the data in the CRS and with the Gender Equality Policy Marker. This has included not only providing overall data but also ranking levels of financing by donor which in turn raises awareness and opens space for dialogue internally for governments t o improve their systems. At CSW 69, the membership convened for the launch of a new dashboard to facilitate both political messages on where needs lie and tracking related to programming. An analytical piece signalling low levels of integration of gender equality in financing for Ukraine was prepared and supported a new Allia nce on Gender-responsive gender equality, part of the Ukraine Reconstruction and Recovery Conference. Page 3 of 3 - Effective support for the implementation of the DAC Recommendation on Ending Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment, as well as expanded adherence by international organisations, development banks, and non -Members. Deliverables include: Overall monitoring survey and report on the implementation of the DAC Recommendation on Ending Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (2024) at the five-year mark since its adoption, and any relevant updating, and support for the DAC Reference Group on Ending SEAH (with DAC GENDERNET) to peer learning on substantive concerns (e.g. links to improving organisational change for gender equality); and a high-level event and continued development of the online space facilitating member exchange to support increased adherence of the DAC Recommendation. The new report on the Implementation of the DAC Recommendation on Ending SEAH adopted by the DAC in July 2024 was used to increase knowledge through, and the Secretariat convened the reference group in November to increase peer learning around areas of accelerated action identified. A new Toolkit on Ending SEAH was completed by the Team and launched in July 2024 as well.
- The development of evidence-based guidance on gender equality and related in-depth analysis on womens economic empowerment and on inequalities that intersect with gender inequality is supporting positive change for development agencies and foreign affairs ministries. Many DAC members have now benefitted from internal workshops developed with the DCD Gender Equality Team and member administrations, reaching from leadership to country offices and partners in civil society and academia to help promote better systems and ultimately gender equality which leads as well to better development outcomes. In some case these were combined with launch sessions for the new DAC Recommendation on Gender Equality and work on the CRS Gender Equality Policy Marker.
- Integration of gender equality into other areas in OECD/DCD: The Secretariat of the GENDERNET and ENVIRONET continued to support and convene the Collaborative on Climate change, Biodiversity and Gender Equality. In 2024, the ground was prepared for a new OECD States of Fragility Report included more gender equalit y factors, building the evidence base. The Secretariat engages as a thought leadership partner with the Women, Peace and Security Compact, and the date on financing for work on WPS were provided as every year to the UN Secretary Generals Report on these issues. Key contribution to a programme for support for Egypt through the OECD Global Relations Directorate with an analytical report prepared by the GEWE Team on financing for gender equality in Egypt. Regular engagement with the Office of the Secretary General on gender equality and engagement in the OECD Ambassadors Group of Friends of Gender Equality. Substantive work on the design of the OECDs first Strategy in Gender Equality and Forum on Gend er Equality.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
